sanskrit: na tv etad anurūpaṃ te yaśaso vā kulasya vā samṛddhārtho 'samṛddhārthaṃ yan māṃ katthitum icchasi
english: Yet this does not befit either your renown or your lineage—that you, whose ends are fulfilled, should wish to taunt me, whose ends are unfulfilled.

sanskrit: na hi duḥkheṣu śocanti na prahṛṣyanti carddhiṣu kṛtaprajñā jñānatṛptāḥ kṣāntāḥ santo manīṣiṇaḥ
english: For in sorrows they do not grieve, nor in prosperities do they exult—those wise and good men whose insight is perfected, who are satisfied in knowledge and patient of heart.

sanskrit: tvaṃ tu prākṛtayā buddhyā puraṃdara vikatthase yadāham iva bhāvī tvaṃ tadā naivaṃ vadiṣyasi
english: But you, Puraṃdara, boast with a common mind; when you shall come to be as I now am, then you will speak no longer in this fashion.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca punar eva tu taṃ śakraḥ prahasann idam abravīt niḥśvasantaṃ yathā nāgaṃ pravyāhārāya bhārata
english: Bhīṣma said: Then once more, O Bhārata, Śakra, laughing, spoke thus to him—who was hissing forth speech like a serpent—provoking him to answer.

sanskrit: yat tad yānasahasreṇa jñātibhiḥ parivāritaḥ lokān pratāpayan sarvān yāsy asmān avitarkayan
english: Once, encircled by your kinsmen with a thousand chariots, you would ride forth scorching all the worlds, holding us as nothing—

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā sukṛpaṇāṃ cemām avasthām ātmano bale jñātimitraparityaktaḥ śocasy āho na śocasi
english: and now, O Bali, beholding this most pitiable condition of your own, forsaken by kinsmen and friends—do you grieve, or do you not grieve?

sanskrit: prītiṃ prāpyātulāṃ pūrvaṃ lokāṃś cātmavaśe sthitān vinipātam imaṃ cādya śocasy āho na śocasi
english: Having of old won matchless delight and held the worlds within your sway, do you now grieve at this downfall, or do you not grieve?

sanskrit: balir uvāca anityam upalakṣyedaṃ kālaparyāyam ātmanaḥ tasmāc chakra na śocāmi sarvaṃ hy evedam antavat
english: Bali said: Perceiving this turning of Time upon myself to be impermanent, therefore, Śakra, I do not grieve; for all this surely has its end.

sanskrit: antavanta ime dehā bhūtānām amarādhipa tena śakra na śocāmi nāparādhād idaṃ mama
english: These bodies of living beings have an end, O lord of the immortals; for that reason, Śakra, I do not grieve, nor is this state of mine the fruit of any wrongdoing.

sanskrit: jīvitaṃ ca śarīraṃ ca pretya vai saha jāyate ubhe saha vivardhete ubhe saha vinaśyataḥ
english: Life and the body, departing hence, are born together; together the two grow, and together the two perish.

sanskrit: tad īdṛśam idaṃ bhāvam avaśaḥ prāpya kevalam yady evam abhijānāmi kā vyathā me vijānataḥ
english: Having come, helpless, merely to such a state of being as this—if I understand it thus, what anguish can there be for me who knows?

sanskrit: bhūtānāṃ nidhanaṃ niṣṭhā srotasām iva sāgaraḥ naitat samyag vijānanto narā muhyanti vajrabhṛt
english: Destruction is the appointed end of beings, as the ocean is the end of rivers; men who rightly understand this are not bewildered, O wielder of the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: ye tv evaṃ nābhijānanti rajomohaparāyaṇāḥ te kṛcchraṃ prāpya sīdanti buddhir yeṣāṃ praṇaśyati
english: But those who do not so understand, given over to passion and delusion, sink down on meeting hardship, they whose discernment is destroyed.

sanskrit: buddhilābhe hi puruṣaḥ sarvaṃ nudati kilbiṣam vipāpmā labhate sattvaṃ sattvasthaḥ saṃprasīdati
english: For on attaining wisdom a man casts off all his taint; freed from evil he gains purity of being, and abiding in that purity he grows wholly serene.

sanskrit: tatas tu ye nivartante jāyante vā punaḥ punaḥ kṛpaṇāḥ paritapyante te 'narthaiḥ paricoditāḥ
english: But those who fall back from it, or are born again and again, the wretched ones, are tormented, driven on by misfortunes.

sanskrit: arthasiddhim anarthaṃ ca jīvitaṃ maraṇaṃ tathā sukhaduḥkhaphalaṃ caiva na dveṣmi na ca kāmaye
english: Success and failure, life and likewise death, and whatever yields the fruit of pleasure or of pain—I neither hate nor desire.

sanskrit: hataṃ hanti hato hy eva yo naro hanti kaṃ cana ubhau tau na vijānīto yaś ca hanti hataś ca yaḥ
english: The man who slays anyone slays one already slain, and himself is already slain; neither of those two understands—neither he who slays nor he who is slain.

sanskrit: hatvā jitvā ca maghavan yaḥ kaś cit puruṣāyate akartā hy eva bhavati kartā tv eva karoti tat
english: Whoever, O Maghavan, plays the man by slaying and conquering, is in truth no doer at all; rather it is the Doer alone who does that deed.

sanskrit: ko hi lokasya kurute vināśaprabhavāv ubhau kṛtaṃ hi tat kṛtenaiva kartā tasyāpi cāparaḥ
english: For who brings about, for the world, both its destruction and its arising? What is done is done by that very doing, and even of that doer there is another beyond.

sanskrit: pṛthivī vāyur ākāśam āpo jyotiś ca pañcamam etadyonīni bhūtāni tatra kā paridevanā
english: Earth, wind, ether, water, and fire as the fifth—from these elements all creatures spring; over that, what room is there for lamentation?

sanskrit: mahāvidyo 'lpavidyaś ca balavān durbalaś ca yaḥ darśanīyo virūpaś ca subhago durbhagaś ca yaḥ
english: The man of great learning and the man of little, the strong and the weak, the fair to look upon and the misshapen, the fortunate and the luckless—

sanskrit: sarvaṃ kālaḥ samādatte gambhīraḥ svena tejasā tasmin kālavaśaṃ prāpte kā vyathā me vijānataḥ
english: Time, profound, gathers all to itself by its own power; when one has come under Time's dominion, what anguish can there be for me who knows?

sanskrit: dagdham evānudahati hatam evānuhanti ca naśyate naṣṭam evāgre labdhavyaṃ labhate naraḥ
english: It burns only what is already burned, and slays only what is already slain; only what is already lost is lost, and a man obtains only what was beforehand his to obtain.

sanskrit: nāsya dvīpaḥ kutaḥ pāraṃ nāvāraḥ saṃpradṛśyate nāntam asya prapaśyāmi vidher divyasya cintayan
english: It has no island—how then a farther shore?—nor is any nearer bank to be seen; pondering it, I behold no end to this divine ordinance.

sanskrit: yadi me paśyataḥ kālo bhūtāni na vināśayet syān me harṣaś ca darpaś ca krodhaś caiva śacīpate
english: If, while I looked on, Time did not destroy created beings, then there might be in me joy and pride and wrath, O lord of Śacī.

sanskrit: tuṣabhakṣaṃ tu māṃ jñātvā praviviktajane gṛhe bibhrataṃ gārdabhaṃ rūpam ādiśya parigarhase
english: But knowing me a husk-eater in a house emptied of people, wearing the form of an ass, you point me out and revile me.

sanskrit: icchann ahaṃ vikuryāṃ hi rūpāṇi bahudhātmanaḥ vibhīṣaṇāni yānīkṣya palāyethās tvam eva me
english: Yet were I to wish it, I could fashion my own self into many shapes—shapes so terrifying that, at the mere sight of them, it is you who would flee from me.

sanskrit: kālaḥ sarvaṃ samādatte kālaḥ sarvaṃ prayacchati kālena vidhṛtaṃ sarvaṃ mā kṛthāḥ śakra pauruṣam
english: Time takes all to itself, Time bestows all; by Time is everything ordained—do not make a show of manly prowess, Śakra.

sanskrit: purā sarvaṃ pravyathate mayi kruddhe puraṃdara avaimi tv asya lokasya dharmaṃ śakra sanātanam
english: Of old, when I was wrathful, O Puraṃdara, all things trembled; yet I know, Śakra, the eternal law that governs this world.

sanskrit: tvam apy evam apekṣasva mātmanā vismayaṃ gamaḥ prabhavaś ca prabhāvaś ca nātmasaṃsthaḥ kadā cana
english: Do you too consider this, and do not yield to self-conceit; neither origin nor might ever rests within oneself.

sanskrit: kaumāram eva te cittaṃ tathaivādya yathā purā samavekṣasva maghavan buddhiṃ vindasva naiṣṭhikīm
english: Your mind is still that of a boy, as much today as it was before; reflect, O Maghavan, and attain the wisdom that is final and resolved.

sanskrit: devā manuṣyāḥ pitaro gandharvoragarākṣasāḥ āsan sarve mama vaśe tat sarvaṃ vettha vāsava
english: Gods, men, the fathers, gandharvas, serpents, and rākṣasas—all were once within my sway; all that you know well, O Vāsava.

sanskrit: namas tasyai diśe 'py astu yasyāṃ vairocano baliḥ iti mām abhyapadyanta buddhimātsaryamohitāḥ
english: "Homage be even to that quarter wherein dwells Bali Vairocana"—thus they would approach me, bewildered by their grudging minds.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ tad anuśocāmi nātmabhraṃśaṃ śacīpate evaṃ me niścitā buddhiḥ śāstus tiṣṭhāmy ahaṃ vaśe
english: I do not lament for that, nor for my own downfall, O lord of Śacī; so settled is my conviction—I abide in the power of the Ruler.

sanskrit: dṛśyate hi kule jāto darśanīyaḥ pratāpavān duḥkhaṃ jīvan sahāmātyo bhavitavyaṃ hi tat tathā
english: For one is seen, born of high family, comely and full of valor, living in misery together with his ministers—because it was destined so to be.

sanskrit: dauṣkuleyas tathā mūḍho durjātaḥ śakra dṛśyate sukhaṃ jīvan sahāmātyo bhavitavyaṃ hi tat tathā
english: And one of mean family, a fool, ill-born, is seen, O Śakra, living in happiness together with his ministers—because it was destined so to be.

sanskrit: kalyāṇī rūpasaṃpannā durbhagā śakra dṛśyate alakṣaṇā virūpā ca subhagā śakra dṛśyate
english: A woman fair and graced with beauty is seen unfortunate, O Śakra; while one without auspicious marks and ill-formed is seen fortunate, O Śakra.

sanskrit: naitad asmatkṛtaṃ śakra naitac chakra tvayā kṛtam yat tvam evaṃgato vajrin yad vāpy evaṃgatā vayam
english: This was not wrought by me, Śakra, nor was this wrought by you, O Śakra—that you have come to such a state, O wielder of the thunderbolt, or that we have come to such a state as this.

sanskrit: na karma tava nānyeṣāṃ kuto mama śatakrato ṛddhir vāpy atha vā narddhiḥ paryāyakṛtam eva tat
english: It is no deed of yours, nor of others—how then of mine, O Śatakratu? Prosperity, or want of prosperity, is wrought merely by the turning of Time.

sanskrit: paśyāmi tvā virājantaṃ devarājam avasthitam śrīmantaṃ dyutimantaṃ ca garjantaṃ ca mamopari
english: I see you shining in splendor, the king of the gods established in your place, glorious and radiant, and thundering over me.

sanskrit: etac caivaṃ na cet kālo mām ākramya sthito bhavet pātayeyam ahaṃ tvādya savajram api muṣṭinā
english: And were it not that Time stands thus, having overpowered me, I would this day strike you down with my fist—thunderbolt and all.

sanskrit: na tu vikramakālo 'yaṃ kṣamākālo 'yam āgataḥ kālaḥ sthāpayate sarvaṃ kālaḥ pacati vai tathā
english: But this is no time for valor; this is the time of forbearance that has come. Time establishes all; Time, even so, ripens all to its consummation.

sanskrit: māṃ ced abhyāgataḥ kālo dānaveśvaram ūrjitam garjantaṃ pratapantaṃ ca kam anyaṃ nāgamiṣyati
english: If Time has come upon me, the mighty lord of the dānavas, thundering and scorching—upon whom else will it not come?

sanskrit: dvādaśānāṃ hi bhavatām ādityānāṃ mahātmanām tejāṃsy ekena sarveṣāṃ devarāja hṛtāni me
english: For the splendors of all twelve of you great-souled Ādityas were once carried off by me single-handed, O king of the gods.

sanskrit: aham evodvahāmy āpo visṛjāmi ca vāsava tapāmi caiva trailokyaṃ vidyotāmy aham eva ca
english: It was I who drew up the waters and I who poured them down, O Vāsava; I who scorched the three worlds, and I alone who gave them light.

sanskrit: saṃrakṣāmi vilumpāmi dadāmy aham athādade saṃyacchāmi niyacchāmi lokeṣu prabhur īśvaraḥ
english: I guarded and I plundered, I gave and I took away, I bound and I restrained—lord and master over all the worlds.

sanskrit: tad adya vinivṛttaṃ me prabhutvam amarādhipa kālasainyāvagāḍhasya sarvaṃ na pratibhāti me
english: All that dominion of mine has now departed, O lord of the immortals; overwhelmed by the armies of Time, nothing of it shines forth for me any more.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ kartā na caiva tvaṃ nānyaḥ kartā śacīpate paryāyeṇa hi bhujyante lokāḥ śakra yadṛcchayā
english: I am not the doer, nor are you, nor is any other the doer, O lord of Śacī; for the worlds are enjoyed in their turn, Śakra, just as it chances.

sanskrit: māsārdhamāsaveśmānam ahorātrābhisaṃvṛtam ṛtudvāraṃ varṣamukham āhur vedavido janāḥ
english: Those who know the Veda call it the dwelling of months and fortnights, enclosed by day and night, having the seasons for its doors and the year for its mouth.

sanskrit: āhuḥ sarvam idaṃ cintyaṃ janāḥ ke cin manīṣayā asyāḥ pañcaiva cintāyāḥ paryeṣyāmi ca pañcadhā
english: Some men, by their reflection, declare all this to be a matter for meditation; and of this fivefold meditation I shall make my inquiry in five ways.

sanskrit: gambhīraṃ gahanaṃ brahma mahat toyārṇavaṃ yathā anādinidhanaṃ cāhur akṣaraṃ param eva ca
english: Brahman is profound and unfathomable, vast as the ocean of waters; and they declare it to be without beginning or end, the imperishable, the supreme.

sanskrit: sattveṣu liṅgam āveśya naliṅgam api tat svayam manyante dhruvam evainaṃ ye narās tattvadarśinaḥ
english: Having entered into creatures as their distinguishing mark, it is yet in itself without mark; the men who perceive the truth hold it to be ever-abiding and eternal.

sanskrit: bhūtānāṃ tu viparyāsaṃ manyate gatavān iti na hy etāvad bhaved gamyaṃ na yasmāt prakṛteḥ paraḥ
english: One thinks, "it has departed," mistaking the transformation of beings for that; but it could not be a thing to be reached merely thus, since it is beyond Nature itself.

sanskrit: gatiṃ hi sarvabhūtānām agatvā kva gamiṣyasi yo dhāvatā na hātavyas tiṣṭhann api na hīyate tam indriyāṇi sarvāṇi nānupaśyanti pañcadhā
english: For it is the goal of all beings; not having reached it, where will you go? It cannot be outrun by one who runs, nor left behind by one who stands still; and the five senses, in any of their five ways, do not perceive it.

sanskrit: āhuś cainaṃ ke cid agniṃ ke cid āhuḥ prajāpatim ṛtumāsārdhamāsāṃś ca divasāṃs tu kṣaṇāṃs tathā
english: Some call it Agni, some call it Prajāpati, and others the seasons, the months, the fortnights, the days, and likewise the moments.

sanskrit: pūrvāhṇam aparāhṇaṃ ca madhyāhnam api cāpare muhūrtam api caivāhur ekaṃ santam anekadhā taṃ kālam avajānīhi yasya sarvam idaṃ vaśe
english: Others call it the forenoon, the afternoon, the midday; yet others call it the muhūrta—calling that which is one by many names. Know that to be Time, in whose power all this lies.

sanskrit: bahūnīndrasahasrāṇi samatītāni vāsava balavīryopapannāni yathaiva tvaṃ śacīpate
english: Many thousands of Indras have passed away, O Vāsava, endowed with strength and valor even as you are, O lord of Śacī.

sanskrit: tvām apy atibalaṃ śakraṃ devarājaṃ balotkaṭam prāpte kāle mahāvīryaḥ kālaḥ saṃśamayiṣyati
english: And you too, O Śakra, exceedingly strong, king of the gods, towering in might—when the hour comes, mighty Time will lay to rest.

sanskrit: ya idaṃ sarvam ādatte tasmāc chakra sthiro bhava mayā tvayā ca pūrvaiś ca na sa śakyo 'tivartitum
english: It is that which seizes all this to itself; therefore, Śakra, be steadfast. By me, by you, and by those before us, it could never be overpassed.

sanskrit: yām etāṃ prāpya jānīṣe rājaśriyam anuttamām sthitā mayīti tan mithyā naiṣā hy ekatra tiṣṭhati
english: This unsurpassed royal Fortune that you have won and think, "she abides in me"—that is false; for she stays nowhere in one place.

sanskrit: sthitā hīndrasahasreṣu tvad viśiṣṭatameṣv iyam māṃ ca lolā parityajya tvām agād vibudhādhipa
english: She has dwelt with thousands of Indras far more distinguished than you; and the fickle one, abandoning me, has gone over to you, O lord of the wise.

sanskrit: maivaṃ śakra punaḥ kārṣīḥ śānto bhavitum arhasi tvām apy evaṃgataṃ tyaktvā kṣipram anyaṃ gamiṣyati
english: Do not act thus again, Śakra; it behooves you to be at peace. Forsaking you too when you have come to such a state, she will swiftly pass on to another.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca śatakratur athāpaśyad baler dīptāṃ mahātmanaḥ svarūpiṇīṃ śarīrād dhi tadā niṣkrāmatīṃ śriyam
english: Bhīṣma said: Then Śatakratu beheld the radiant Fortune of the great-souled Bali, in her own embodied form, even then departing from his body.

sanskrit: tāṃ dīptāṃ prabhayā dṛṣṭvā bhagavān pākaśāsanaḥ vismayotphullanayano baliṃ papraccha vāsavaḥ
english: Seeing her shining with such brilliance, the blessed Pākaśāsana, the lord Vāsava, his eyes wide with wonder, questioned Bali.

sanskrit: bale keyam apakrāntā rocamānā śikhaṇḍinī tvattaḥ sthitā sakeyūrā dīpyamānā svatejasā
english: "O Bali, who is this crested one, gleaming and beautiful, who has stepped forth from you and stands there, adorned with armlets, blazing with her own splendor?"

sanskrit: balir uvāca na hīmām āsurīṃ vedmi na daivīṃ na ca mānuṣīm tvam evaināṃ pṛccha mā vā yatheṣṭaṃ kuru vāsava
english: Bali said: I know her neither as an asura-woman, nor divine, nor human; question her yourself, or do not—do as you please, O Vāsava.

sanskrit: śakra uvāca kā tvaṃ baler apakrāntā rocamānā śikhaṇḍinī ajānato mamācakṣva nāmadheyaṃ śucismite
english: Śakra said: Who are you, O crested and gleaming one, who have stepped forth from Bali? Tell me, who do not know it, your name, O you of bright smile.

sanskrit: kā tvaṃ tiṣṭhasi māyeva dīpyamānā svatejasā hitvā daityeśvaraṃ subhru tan mamācakṣva tattvataḥ
english: Who are you that stand there like an apparition, blazing with your own splendor, having forsaken the lord of the daityas, O fair-browed one? Tell me that in truth.

sanskrit: śrīr uvāca na mā virocano veda na mā vairocano baliḥ āhur māṃ duḥsahety evaṃ vidhitseti ca māṃ viduḥ
english: Śrī said: Neither Virocana knew me, nor Bali Vairocana; they call me Duḥsahā, the Unendurable, and they know me too as Vidhitsā, the Will-to-ordain.

sanskrit: bhūtir lakṣmīti mām āhuḥ śrīr ity evaṃ ca vāsava tvaṃ māṃ śakra na jānīṣe sarve devā na māṃ viduḥ
english: They call me Bhūti and Lakṣmī, and Śrī as well, O Vāsava; you, Śakra, do not know me, and all the gods know me not.

sanskrit: śakra uvāca kim idaṃ tvaṃ mama kṛte utāho balinaḥ kṛte duḥsahe vijahāsy enaṃ cirasaṃvāsinī satī
english: Śakra said: Why is this, O Duḥsahā—is it for my sake, or is it for Bali's sake that you forsake him, you who have dwelt with him so long?

sanskrit: śrīr uvāca na dhātā na vidhātā māṃ vidadhāti kathaṃ cana kālas tu śakra paryāyān mainaṃ śakrāvamanyathāḥ
english: Śrī said: Neither the Ordainer nor the Disposer disposes of me in any way; it is Time, Śakra, working through its turnings. Do not, O Śakra, despise him for this.

sanskrit: śakra uvāca kathaṃ tvayā balis tyaktaḥ kimarthaṃ vā śikhaṇḍini kathaṃ ca māṃ na jahyās tvaṃ tan me brūhi śucismite
english: Śakra said: How was Bali forsaken by you, and for what cause, O crested one? And how would you not forsake me too? Tell me that, O you of bright smile.

sanskrit: śrīr uvāca satye sthitāsmi dāne ca vrate tapasi caiva hi parākrame ca dharme ca parācīnas tato baliḥ
english: Śrī said: I rest in truth, in giving, in the keeping of vows, in austerity, in valor, and in dharma; but Bali has turned away from these—therefore I have left him.

sanskrit: brahmaṇyo 'yaṃ sadā bhūtvā satyavādī jitendriyaḥ abhyasūyad brāhmaṇān vai ucchiṣṭaś cāspṛśad ghṛtam
english: Having ever been devoted to the brahmans, truthful of speech, his senses subdued, he came to spite the brahmans, and, defiled by leavings, he touched the clarified butter.

sanskrit: yajñaśīlaḥ purā bhūtvā mām eva yajatety ayam provāca lokān mūḍhātmā kālenopanipīḍitaḥ
english: Having of old been devoted to sacrifice, this man, his soul deluded and oppressed by Time, declared to the worlds, "Worship me alone."

sanskrit: apākṛtā tataḥ śakra tvayi vatsyāmi vāsava apramattena dhāryāsmi tapasā vikrameṇa ca
english: Cast off from him, then, O Śakra, I shall dwell in you, O Vāsava; but I must be upheld by one ever-heedful, through austerity and through valor.

sanskrit: śakra uvāca asti devamanuṣyeṣu sarvabhūteṣu vā pumān yas tvām eko viṣahituṃ śaknuyāt kamalālaye
english: Śakra said: Is there among gods and men, or among all beings, any single man able to bear you alone, O dweller in the lotus?

sanskrit: śrīr uvāca naiva devo na gandharvo nāsuro na ca rākṣasaḥ yo mām eko viṣahituṃ śaktaḥ kaś cit puraṃdara
english: Śrī said: Neither god, nor gandharva, nor asura, nor rākṣasa—there is none, O Puraṃdara, who is able to bear me alone.

sanskrit: śakra uvāca tiṣṭhethā mayi nityaṃ tvaṃ yathā tad brūhi me śubhe tat kariṣyāmi te vākyam ṛtaṃ tvaṃ vaktum arhasi
english: Śakra said: Tell me, O blessed one, in what manner you might abide in me forever; that word of yours I shall fulfill—and it behooves you to speak the truth.
